adjudication.rationale: In app/models/topic_embed.rb, TopicEmbed.import appends HTML containing an #{url} constructed via string interpolation after only checking `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`. adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, feed item content is processed as `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then passed into `TopicEmbed.import(...)`. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for `:raw_html` (skipping the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline). The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked`. This means HTML entities in feeds (e.g. `<script>`) are decoded into live tags before being stored/rendered, enabling injection/XSS via feed content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:31-35 accesses nil fields: i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError for description-only items, a nil url (missing/relative link and nil id, since RSS 2.0 exposes guid not id) raises on NilClass in the ^https? check, and a nil title reaches PostCreator with skip_validations: true
matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly notes that `i.content.scrub` can raise `NoMethodError` for items that only have `description` (i.e., `i.content` is nil), which is the same core issue as the golden comment’s missing-content-field crash and need for a fallback. अतिरिक्त issues mentioned don’t change that it identifies the same underlying bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed has no per-item rescue and sidekiq_options retry: false, so the first bad item aborts the run and, because feed order is stable, crashes every hourly run, meaning every item after it is never imported

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `sidekiq_options retry: false` is set and `poll_feed` iterates `rss.items.each` without any per-item exception handling. Several per-item operations can raise (e.g., `i.content.scrub` if `i.content` is nil, `CGI.unescapeHTML` on non-strings, or unexpected item structure), which would abort the whole job run. Since the job is scheduled hourly and there is no checkpointing/"last processed" tracking, a consistently bad feed entry can cause the job to fail every hour before reaching later items, preventing subsequent items from being imported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: String#scrub requires Ruby >= 2.1; on Ruby 2.0, which Discourse targeted at this time, it raises NoMethodError even for valid strings

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an unconditional call to `String#scrub` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` (`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`). If `scrub` is not defined on `String` in the runtime, this will raise `NoMethodError` and break feed polling/importing. The diff provides no fallback/guard around `scrub`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: import_remote calls open(url).read with no scheme/host validation; Kernel#open treats a string beginning with '|' as a command to execute, so a crafted thread link in a Disqus export file yields command execution on the server during an admin-run import (TopicRetriever is safe only because it validates the host against embeddable_host first)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import_remote, the diff introduces `open(url).read` with no validation of `url` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). In Ruby, `Kernel#open` treats strings starting with `|` as a command pipeline, so a crafted `t[:link]` from the Disqus export could lead to command execution when `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`. TopicRetriever is comparatively protected by `invalid_host?` rejecting invalid URIs/hosts before calling `import_remote`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls mangles scheme-relative URLs: '//cdn.example/x.jpg' matches start_with?('/'), has all leading slashes stripped, and gets the article host prefixed, producing http://articlehost/cdn.example/x.jpg — a broken URL pointing at the wrong host

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')` is rewritten as `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"` (and same for `src`). Scheme-relative URLs like `'//cdn.example/x.jpg'` also start with `'/'`, so all leading slashes are stripped to `'cdn.example/x.jpg'` and then the article host prefix is prepended, producing `http://<articlehost>/cdn.example/x.jpg`, which is a broken URL pointing at the wrong host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls ignores relative URLs without a leading slash (e.g. 'img/x.png'), which are not absolutized at all and resolve against the forum's URL when the post is rendered, producing broken images/links in imported content

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls, only links/images whose href/src start with '/' are rewritten (e.g. `if href.present? && href.start_with?('/')`). Relative URLs like `img/x.png`, `./img/x.png`, or `../img/x.png` are left untouched, despite the method comment claiming to convert relative URLs to absolute. That would cause imported HTML to render those resources relative to the Discourse forum/page instead of the source site, breaking images/links.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js:16 uses discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1, a substring test rather than an exact origin match, so an attacker at e.g. https://forum.example.co passes when the forum is https://forum.example.com and can forge discourse-resize messages to manipulate the embedded iframe's height
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same flaw: using `indexOf`/substring matching for origin validation instead of an exact origin comparison, which can be bypassed by attacker-controlled domains that contain/closely resemble the trusted domain (e.g., evil-<trusted>.com or forum.example.co vs forum.example.com).

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_retriever.rb:27-29 uses non-atomic SETNX followed by EXPIRE; if the process dies between them the retrieved:<url> key persists with no TTL, so retrieved_recently? returns true forever and non-staff-triggered retrieval for that embed_url never runs again — should use a single atomic SET key value NX EX 60

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle logic does `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` followed by `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. This two-step pattern is not atomic: if the process/thread dies after SETNX succeeds but before EXPIRE runs, the `retrieved:<embed_url>` key can persist without a TTL. After that, future calls will see setnx fail and treat it as "retrieved recently" indefinitely (for non-staff, since staff bypasses the throttle), preventing retrieval from ever running again for that URL. Using a single atomic `SET key value NX EX 60` (or equivalent) would avoid the stuck-key condition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embeds rows are never cleaned up when the associated topic or post is deleted (no dependent: handling or callbacks), so topic_id_for_embed keeps returning the stale id, the controller builds a TopicView for a deleted topic instead of falling through to re-import, TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve early-returns, and a hard-deleted post crashes the update path via PostRevisor.new(nil)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed` records with `belongs_to :topic` and `belongs_to :post` but no `dependent:` cleanup, callbacks, or DB-level foreign keys/cascades (migration only adds a unique index on `embed_url`). `topic_id_for_embed` blindly plucks `topic_id`, and `EmbedController#best` treats any returned id as valid (`TopicView.new(topic_id, ...)`) rather than falling back to re-import. Separately, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` early-returns if any `TopicEmbed` row exists for the URL, even if its `topic_id/post_id` now point to deleted rows. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then `PostRevisor.new(post)`; if the post was hard-deleted, `embed.post` is nil and this would likely raise. These are concrete stale-association failure modes grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Unbounded Sidekiq job enqueue per page view in embed_controller.rb:15 — every request for a not-yet-imported URL unconditionally enqueues a retrieve_topic job with no dedup before enqueue; the 30-second auto-reload in loading.html.erb generates ~2 jobs/minute per visitor, and failed imports (retry: false) never resolve the loop, producing an unbounded stream of mostly-no-op jobs and Redis writes

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url) is nil, it unconditionally enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) on every request before rendering the loading view. loading.html.erb auto-reloads every 30s, so a visitor can trigger repeated enqueues until the embed is imported. While TopicRetriever#retrieve has a Redis-based throttle (retrieved_recently?) that makes the job mostly a no-op, it does not prevent the Sidekiq queue from accumulating redundant jobs (no dedup before enqueue). Parts of the finding about “retry: false” apply to PollFeed (sidekiq_options retry: false), not RetrieveTopic, but the core unbounded enqueue concern is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Full feed poll executed synchronously inside a page-view-triggered job in lib/topic_retriever.rb:38 — perform_retrieve calls Jobs::PollFeed inline with no distributed lock, so concurrent retrieve_topic jobs each run the full poll and losers raise on the unique embed_url index after wasting duplicate PostCreator work, turning a user request into an O(feed size) workload with unbounded concurrency

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline before doing `fetch_http`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` iterates the entire RSS feed and calls `TopicEmbed.import` per item, which can create a Topic+Post and then `TopicEmbed.create!` under a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url`. There is no distributed lock around the poll (and TopicRetriever’s redis throttle is only per `@embed_url`, not global), so concurrent `retrieve_topic` jobs can redundantly poll the full feed and race on creating the same `embed_url`, causing uniqueness exceptions and wasted PostCreator work. This is a correctness/reliability issue exposed by the diff, not just style.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: poll_feed processes the entire feed with no item cap in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:32 — rss.items.each imports every item via TopicEmbed.import and PostCreator on first run, with no batch limit or incremental import, hammering the DB and queue for the duration on large feeds

adjudication.rationale: In app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb, `poll_feed` does `rss.items.each do |i| ... TopicEmbed.import(...) end` with no limit, pagination, or “only new items since X” logic. The diff shows no use of `feed_key` (defined but unused) or any modified-since/ETag caching, so on a large feed the job can import every item (creating/updating topics/posts) in a single run, which is a concrete performance/operational concern introduced by this change rather than a direct correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: No timeout or size limit on outbound HTTP fetches in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:30 and app/models/topic_embed.rb:45 — bare open-uri calls without read_timeout/open_timeout buffer entire responses into memory, allowing a slow or hung remote host to pin a Sidekiq worker indefinitely and stack hung hourly PollFeed runs that starve the worker pool

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new outbound HTTP fetches using bare `open-uri` with no timeouts or response size limits: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote`. Both can block a Sidekiq worker indefinitely on slow/hung hosts and `open(url).read` buffers the full response into memory, creating a real availability/resource-exhaustion risk in these background jobs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: add_column with null: false + default in db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 rewrites the entire posts table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on PostgreSQL < 11, blocking all reads and writes on large forums; the nullable add → batched backfill → set not null pattern is not used

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `AddCookMethodToPosts` that does `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. On PostgreSQL versions prior to 11, adding a column with a non-null default is known to rewrite the whole table and take an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock, which can block reads/writes on large `posts` tables. The finding correctly points out the safer pattern (nullable add → backfill → set default/not null) is not used. This is an operational/performance risk rather than an app correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: feed_key in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20 is dead code — the Redis key intended for ETag/Last-Modified conditional fetching is never referenced, so every hourly run re-downloads the full feed and re-hashes/looks-up every item even when nothing changed

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the `feed_key` method (building a Redis key from `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`) is defined but never called from `execute` or `poll_feed` (or anywhere else in this diff). The job always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and iterates `rss.items` each run, with no Redis/ETag/Last-Modified conditional-fetch logic. This is a real, diff-grounded inefficiency/dead-code concern, but not a correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P0: `cooked` no longer sanitized for `cook_method = raw_html` posts — import paths (PollFeed, import_remote) feed untrusted external content into `cooked` with no sanitization, breaking the public API contract that `cooked` is sanitized HTML and enabling stored XSS via feed content like `

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline and the `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` hook. `TopicEmbed.import` and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` set `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and populate `raw` from externally sourced HTML (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` in `Jobs::PollFeed`, and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `import_remote`) with no sanitization step. The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`), so any unsafe HTML in the feed/article will be output directly, enabling stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Unescaped URL interpolated into an HTML attribute in `TopicEmbed.import` (`"#{url}") — url is only gated by `/^https?\:\/\//` so quotes/angle brackets are permitted, allowing a feed `` like `http://host/x'>` to break out of the attribute and inject stored HTML/XSS from the URL field alone

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends raw HTML containing an `` built from `url` after only checking `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` (allows quotes/`>` etc.): `contents << "...#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")}`. This HTML is then saved via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for `:raw_html`. The embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. Therefore a crafted URL (from feed `i.link` in `Jobs::PollFeed` or from `embed_url` in `TopicRetriever` -> `import_remote`) can break out of the attribute and inject stored HTML/JS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: `disqus:import` CLI contract break — the `--category`/`-c` option was removed from the public, documented migration task with no deprecation or alias, so existing scripts passing `-c` will fail (thor rejects unknown switches) and category assignment is silently dropped from output

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the public Thor option `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` was removed, along with the logic that looked up `category_id` and passed it into `PostCreator` (`category: category_id`). The task now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` with no category support. This is a backwards-incompatible CLI change: existing invocations that pass `-c/--category` will fail because Thor rejects unknown switches, and category assignment behavior is removed with no alias/deprecation shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: `disqus:import` behavior/data drift — the task now requires a live HTTP fetch of `t[:link]` for every thread via `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, so unreachable/blank links raise and abort the whole import mid-run, original post dates (`created_at`) are lost (posts dated at import time), and Disqus-hosted links import garbage page content, changing output data shape and failure semantics for existing callers without notice

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import loop no longer uses `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) ...)` and instead calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not pass through `created_at` at all, so imported topics/posts will be timestamped at import time (data drift/loss of original dates). Also, `TopicEmbed.import_remote` performs `open(url).read` with no rescue; any network/HTTP/URI error during a single thread fetch will raise and can abort the whole Thor task mid-run, changing failure semantics from the previous offline-safe creation. These issues are directly evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: `/embed/best` lets unauthenticated callers trigger outbound fetches and unlimited topic creation — the referer check is trivially forged and the throttle key is per-URL only (`retrieved:<embed_url>`), so an attacker cycling unique paths on `embeddable_host` bypasses it entirely, causing Sidekiq flooding, fetch amplification against the embeddable host, and unbounded DB/forum spam via auto-created topics/posts with `skip_validations: true`; no global rate limit or caller consideration on the new public endpoint

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new public GET route `get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'` which, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ... embed_url: embed_url)` (EmbedController#best). `ensure_embeddable` only checks `request.referer` host equals `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and this header can be trivially spoofed by a direct caller; there is no authentication or global rate limiting shown. The job executes `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, whose throttle is per full URL key `retrieved:#{@embed_url}` for 60s, so an attacker can bypass by cycling unique paths on the allowed host. Each unique URL can lead to `TopicEmbed.import_remote` fetching `open(url).read` and then `TopicEmbed.import` creating a new topic/post with `PostCreator.new(... skip_validations: true, cook_method: ... )`, and `topic_embeds.embed_url` is only unique per URL, allowing unbounded topic creation across many URLs. This matches the finding’s DoS/spam risk grounded in the added code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Embed "loading" page has no terminal state — if the topic is never created (fetch failure, non-HTML page, or the referer-host vs embed_url-host validation mismatch between the controller and TopicRetriever, e.g. `www.example.com` vs `example.com` misconfiguration), every viewer reloads every 30 seconds forever and each reload enqueues another job that can never succeed, causing unbounded client polling and job spam on a public endpoint with no error surfaced to the integrator

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `TopicEmbed` exists it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The `loading.html.erb` then `document.location.reload()` every 30s with no stop condition or error state, so viewers will hit `embed/best` repeatedly until an embed exists. Each hit re-enqueues another `retrieve_topic` job, even if retrieval can never succeed (e.g., controller only validates `request.referer` host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, while `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` validates the *embed_url* host against the same setting; a `www.` vs bare-domain mismatch would pass the controller but make `TopicRetriever` permanently no-op). This creates an infinite client reload loop and unbounded job enqueuing on a public endpoint when retrieval fails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: `PollFeed` assumes Atom-style item fields — `i.content.scrub` has no nil guard (RSS 2.0 description-only feeds and Atom entries without `content` yield nil/undefined) and `i.id` assumes Atom (RSS uses `guid`), so common feeds crash the job, and with `sidekiq_options retry: false` the same item fails again every hourly run, permanently disabling feed import despite advertised "RSS or ATOM" support

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job unconditionally does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`; if `i.content` is `nil` for a feed item, this will raise (e.g., `NoMethodError` on `nil.scrub`) and crash the poll. The URL fallback also assumes `i.id` (`url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`), which may not exist for some RSS items. Since the job has `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a crash won’t be retried by Sidekiq, but the scheduled job will keep failing on subsequent hourly runs, effectively breaking feed import until data/settings change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: `absolutize_urls` raises on unparseable URLs — `URI(url)` at `app/models/topic_embed.rb:56` is unrescued, so a feed link like `http://foo bar` passes the `^https?\:\/\//` regex check but raises `URI::InvalidURIError` (unlike `TopicRetriever`, which rescues it), killing the import

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the only URL validation is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which would still accept strings like `http://foo bar`. The method then calls `absolutize_urls(url, contents)`, and `absolutize_urls` does `uri = URI(url)` with no rescue for `URI::InvalidURIError`. A malformed-but-regex-matching URL would therefore raise and abort the import/polling job, unlike `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` which explicitly rescues invalid URIs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: New public `embed.js` snippet requires an undocumented trailing slash on `discourseUrl` — `discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."` produces `/embedbest` → 404 if `discourseUrl` lacks a trailing slash, with no validation or fallback, making the new public embed contract fragile with implicit preconditions (trailing slash, required `discourse-comments` element and globals) that silently produce broken embeds

adjudication.rationale: In new `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, `iframe.src` is built via string concatenation: `discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."`. If `discourseUrl` does not end with `/`, the resulting URL becomes malformed (e.g. `https://forum.example.comembed/best?...`), breaking the embed. The diff does not add any normalization/validation (e.g. ensuring a trailing slash) or fallback, so this fragile implicit precondition is introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Imported third-party HTML bypasses the entire sanitize/cook pipeline (stored XSS): cook returns raw verbatim when cook_method == raw_html, feed/article HTML is stored as post content with no sanitization, and the 'imported from' footer interpolates url unescaped into HTML, so script/event-handler markup from feeds or embeddable hosts is stored and rendered as-is

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a `raw_html` cook method that returns `raw` verbatim (`Post#cook`: `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. New imports use this mode: `TopicEmbed.import` calls `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), ... cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], skip_validations: true)`, and `Jobs::PollFeed` feeds `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` into `TopicEmbed.import` without any sanitization. The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`), so any script/event-handler HTML from feeds/remote pages would be stored and rendered. Additionally, `imported_from` builds an HTML `` with `url` interpolated into single-quoted attributes (`"#{url}"`) after only a loose `^https?://` check, allowing attribute injection via quotes in the URL. This is a concrete stored-XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed has no per-item error handling: i.content.scrub raises NoMethodError for feeds lacking an Atom-style <content> element (plain RSS 2.0 uses description/content:encoded), nil titles hit the PostCreator NOT NULL constraint, URI(url) raises for URLs passing the loose /^https?\:\/\// guard, and URLs longer than the 255-char embed_url column raise on insert — any of these aborts the items loop mid-feed, and with retry: false and hourly recurrence the job re-fails at the same item every hour with no rescue or logging

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop does `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and then `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, i.title, content)` with no per-item rescue. If a feed item lacks `content` (common for RSS 2.0 which may use `description`/`content:encoded`), `i.content` can be `nil` and `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting the entire job mid-feed. Additionally, `TopicEmbed.import` only guards URLs with `/^https?\:\/\//`, but then calls `absolutize_urls(url, contents)` which does `URI(url)` without rescue; a syntactically invalid URL that still matches the regex would raise and similarly kill the job. Given `sidekiq_options retry: false` and hourly recurrence, the scheduled job would keep failing on the problematic item without progressing or logging.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No timeouts on outbound HTTP fetches: open(url).read in topic_embed.rb import_remote and open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) in poll_feed.rb pass no open_timeout/read_timeout, so a stalled or malicious remote host parks a Sidekiq thread for minutes or indefinitely — compounded by PollFeed being executed synchronously inside user-triggered RetrieveTopic jobs, allowing hung hourly runs to accumulate and starve Sidekiq concurrency

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces outbound HTTP fetches via Ruby's `open` without any timeout controls: `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)` in `app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote` and `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb#poll_feed`. Additionally, `lib/topic_retriever.rb#perform_retrieve` runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously inside the user-triggered `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` path (`app/jobs/regular/retrieve_topic.rb`), so a stalled remote host can block a Sidekiq worker thread, potentially causing queue starvation. This is a concrete availability/security defect grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Retrieval path fails silently with no terminal state or circuit breaker: fetch_http silently returns when embed_by_username doesn't resolve to a user, silently no-ops when the embed_url host doesn't match embeddable_host (a deterministic dead end since the controller validates only the referer host), and the loading page reloads every 30 seconds indefinitely with each reload enqueuing another RetrieveTopic job — producing an infinite request/job cycle with no backoff, negative-result caching, or error shown to the viewer

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an embed loading loop with no terminal failure handling. In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil it always enqueues `:retrieve_topic` then renders `loading` (`app/controllers/embed_controller.rb`). The loading template reloads every 30s (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`), so each reload triggers another enqueue, potentially forever. Meanwhile `TopicRetriever#retrieve` can deterministically no-op: `invalid_host?` rejects when `URI(@embed_url).host` != `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (`lib/topic_retriever.rb`), but the controller only validates the **referer** host (`ensure_embeddable`), not `embed_url`, so a mismatched `embed_url` yields a permanent dead end. Also `fetch_http` returns if `embed_by_username` doesn’t resolve to a user, with no error surfaced, leaving the client stuck on perpetual reload. Although `retrieved_recently?` throttles actual retrieval attempts, it does not prevent repeated job enqueues/requests or provide a terminal state/error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled fetch/parse exceptions in the retrieval job: open(url) raises OpenURI::HTTPError, Errno::ECONNREFUSED, and timeout errors, and Readability raises on non-HTML payloads, but nothing is rescued in Jobs::RetrieveTopic — with Sidekiq's default retry: true, a permanently broken URL (404, non-HTML page) is re-fetched ~25 times over several weeks with no logging to distinguish transient from permanent failures

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE throttle can permanently wedge retrieval for a URL: if the process dies between setnx and expire, the retrieved:<url> key persists with no TTL and retrieved_recently? returns true forever, so that embed URL can never be fetched again without manual Redis cleanup — SET key "1" EX 60 NX is atomic and eliminates the window

This is non-atomic and creates a real failure window: if the process crashes after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the `retrieved:<url>` key will remain without a TTL. Subsequent calls will see `setnx` fail and return `true` (treated as "retrieved recently") forever, preventing future retrieval for that embed URL until manual Redis cleanup. Using an atomic `SET ... NX EX 60` would eliminate this wedge.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No cleanup or handling when an embedded topic/post is deleted: TopicEmbed has no dependent handling, topic_id_for_embed keeps returning the deleted topic's id so TopicView.new errors and every embed view 500s indefinitely, and embed.post is nil after post deletion causing PostRevisor.new(nil) to raise NoMethodError, which also breaks subsequent feed polls for that URL

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic setnx + expire throttle key in TopicRetriever can stick forever: if the process dies between $redis.setnx and $redis.expire, the retrieved:<url> key persists indefinitely and that embed URL can never be retrieved again; use SET key val EX 60 NX

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook_method: raw_html makes Post#cook return raw verbatim with no markdown pipeline, no after_post_cook filters, and no sanitization; the raw value is then rendered with <%= raw post.cooked %> in the embed view and treated as trusted HTML everywhere else (topic pages, emails), enabling stored XSS from external content in the forum origin

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed feeds CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) straight in, double-decoding the feed so entity-escaped HTML (including <script>, onerror= handlers, javascript: hrefs) that any normal feed legitimately escapes becomes live markup

adjudication_records.issue_text: import_remote's readability whitelist (tags/attributes) strips on* handlers but still passes javascript: hrefs
